successCriteria.description: The Notification entity type is exported from the notification module and exposes the lifecycle status type covering exactly PENDING, SENT, READ, ARCHIVED.

The notification repository persists a notification via create and returns the created Notification with DB-assigned createdAt; findByRecipient returns all notifications for a given recipient; markSent transitions status to SENT and markRead transitions status to READ and sets readAt, both returning the updated Notification or null when no row matches.

The notification service notify(recipientId, type, title, message, relatedEntityType?, relatedEntityId?) creates a notification with status PENDING, defaults relatedEntityType and relatedEntityId to null when omitted, generates a unique id, delegates persistence to the injected repository, and returns the resulting Notification.
The notification service does not import or reference the database pool directly; all persistence is delegated to the injected INotificationRepository (constructor injection).

The notification module barrel (index.ts) re-exports the Notification entity, the NotificationStatus type, the repository interface and class, and the service interface and class, so downstream modules import only through the barrel.

Jest unit tests at tests/unit/modules/notification/notification.service.test.ts cover notify creating a PENDING notification with defaulted null related-entity fields, passing the generated id and supplied fields to the repository, and returning the repository result; the test mocks the repository (not the pool).

constraints: No use of `any` — use `unknown` with type guards (HARNESS constraint no-any, tsconfig strict).

No direct database access outside the repository — the service must not import or use the pool; all DB access goes through INotificationRepository (GP-001, HARNESS constraint no-direct-db-outside-repository).
Repository queries must use parameterised queries only (no string-interpolated values) and set createdAt via NOW() with RETURNING *, matching the employee/policy repository convention.
Modules import from each other only through their declared public entry point (index.ts barrel); no imports of another module's internals (AGENTS.md architecture rule 1).
No unhandled promise rejections — all async errors in the service and repository are propagated as rejected promises, not swallowed (GP-006).
No hardcoded secrets, passwords, API keys, or tokens (HARNESS constraint no-hardcoded-secrets).
outOfScope: Controller, routes, and HTTP/RBAC wiring for the notification module — deferred to later controller/routes phases.
Zod validation schemas for notification inputs — deferred to the validation-schemas phase.
Repository unit tests (notification.repository.test.ts) — this phase only requires the service test; repository tests are not mandated by the phase scope.
Adding NotificationStatus to src/shared/types/index.ts — it is defined locally in notification.model.ts per the settled decision.
Actual notification delivery (email/push/fanout via BullMQ) — this phase only creates and persists the notification record; delivery is out of scope.

entityInvariants.invariant: A newly created Notification always starts in the PENDING status with readAt null; status may only advance through the defined sequence PENDING → SENT → READ, with ARCHIVED as a terminal disposition.
readAt is null until the notification is marked READ; marking read sets both status to READ and readAt to the current timestamp.

A Notification is always scoped to exactly one recipient (recipientId is non-null); relatedEntityType and relatedEntityId are either both null or both set, linking the notification to an optional domain entity.

interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Rejects the promise on DB errors (e.g. constraint violations); never swallows. createdAt is DB-assigned via NOW(), not caller-supplied.
Returns an empty array (not null) when no notifications exist for the recipient; rejects the promise on DB errors.
Returns the updated Notification with status SENT, or null when no row matches the id; rejects the promise on DB errors.
Returns the updated Notification with status READ and readAt set, or null when no row matches the id; rejects the promise on DB errors.

interfaceConstraints.operation: notificationService.notify(recipientId, type, title, message, relatedEntityType?, relatedEntityId?)
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Generates a unique id, sets status PENDING, defaults omitted related-entity params to null, delegates to repository.create, and returns the persisted Notification; propagates repository errors as rejected promises.

consistencyRequirements.requirement: The NotificationRepository must follow the established repository pattern: import pool from shared/db/connection, define a standalone INotificationRepository interface, use a private snake_case row interface with a mapRowToNotification mapper, use parameterised queries with NOW() and RETURNING *, and return Notification | null from update-style methods (markSent/markRead) — matching the employee repository's create/update/softDelete conventions.

The Notification model interface must be a standalone camelCase interface (not extending BaseEntity), matching the employee and policy model convention; NotificationStatus is defined locally in notification.model.ts as a string-literal union, not imported from shared types.

The notification barrel (index.ts) must re-export the model, repository interface + class, and service interface + class from their respective files, matching the employee/policy barrel export pattern.

The NotificationService must follow the established service pattern: a standalone INotificationService interface and a NotificationService class implementing it in a single service file, receiving its dependency (INotificationRepository) via constructor injection — matching the status service interface+class split and the constructor-injection convention.

The notification service test must follow the established Jest test conventions: file named *.test.ts under tests/unit/modules/notification/, bare module paths (e.g. modules/notification/...) enabled by jest.config moduleDirectories ['node_modules','src'], and mocking the injected repository (INotificationRepository) rather than the pool — matching how the employee test mocks its dependency.

The notification module's dependency direction must match the reconciled architecture: notification depends only on src/shared/types/ and src/shared/db/ — it must not import employee, policy, balance, audit, or leave modules (notification is an independent mid-layer module).

integrationPoints.why: The leave orchestrator will inject INotificationService to send notifications to a manager on submission and to the employee on approve/reject; this phase must expose a stable notify(...) service interface and barrel export for that downstream consumption.
The NotificationRepository imports the pg Pool from the shared DB connection to execute parameterised queries against the notifications table.
The notification module depends on Phase 1 shared types; NotificationStatus is defined locally but the module must not duplicate or contradict the canonical shared enums.
